video_title: Wemby PROVED He's Ready for the Moment?? + Spurs-Thunder Predictions

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Castle's amazing motor and impact in the playoffs
quotes.quote: I think he's been amazing on both ends of the floor. This guy just has a motor. He plays hard. He tries to make the right plays. It feels like he's just always in the game in some capacity. And you love to have a young player like that that just knows how to impact the game, whether he's going to score, get stops, dive into the stands, be tough, he's going to argue with people. All of this is just, all of these are just motor plays. Look, this is bully ball right here. He's not going to leave without it.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Castle's playoff growth and San Antonio's confidence
quotes.quote: I love it. He's been great in this postseason. And sometimes you want your young players in this position to just be able, you want to watch them grow and be able to be mature enough to be able to give you the production that he's been able to give you. But he's been above and beyond. Almost averaging 20 points a game. So when everybody starts talking about playoff experience and this and that, at some points you got to create it. You got to start somewhere and it's happening. And I like the fact that Wemby set the tone for this. Like, hey, these teams don't have a lot of experience either. So what's the difference? And I think San Antonio has taken advantage of that. They're well respected, they're well coached, and these guys have a hell of a lot of confidence going into this next round. But Stephon Castle has been able to benefit the most from playing next to the alien and Victor Wembanyama and just being able to do everything that's needed that he doesn't do.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Castle's remarkable two-way impact in the playoffs
quotes.quote: I just like when I see a young dude like this just up his game even more in the postseason. It is insane. The impact that he's had all year long has been just remarkable, right? With defensively, just dogging dudes, 94 feet, picking them up, while still running this offense in the half court and transition, and he's continued to get and work on his outside shot. Now he's coming to way more consistent, reliable three-point shooter. So, he's made the jump from 16 and a half points to 20 points in the postseason, when it matters the most, when it's pressure packed, when your team needs you to survive and advance. This kid has been unbelievable, and he's not just a one-sided player. He's one of the best two-way players that we have in the game, and he's 21 years old. It really is crazy. He's the perfect fit with Wemby. He's the perfect fit with these other guards like Fox and Harper because he does what they do not do and what most guards don't do, and that's rebound, block shots, and defend one through four. It's ridiculous.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Wemby's readiness for the Western Conference Finals matchup
quotes.quote: I think it matters when the matchup that they have. And again, this is the teams, the two teams that if we would have fast-forwarded the season five months ago, this is what we thought, this is what everyone wanted, this is what the people wanted. We got Spurs, Thunder, both the youngest, best, up-and-coming, and they've arrived teams that we have in the NBA. And they're both so special, they're so deep. This is exactly the series in the Western Conference Finals that we wanted. Wemby's going to have to be great. This is a great opportunity for them as underdogs to step up, take that non-experience against the defending champs and do what they do. And again, this is going to take everybody. Guys like Champagnie and Harrison Barnes, like their number's going to get called. It's not just going to be Wemby and Castle and Fox and Harper. Everyone is going to have to collectively be great. But obviously everything goes through him. We know his impact on the defensive end, but he's got to stay out of foul trouble. He's got to be aggressive early. Like how he set the tone in those Game 1s and the All-Star game even, I need that in Game 1 of the Western Conference Finals.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Playoff experience and OKC's confidence against San Antonio
quotes.quote: With all of those guys that Chandler mentioned, and when you start talking about experience, right? The deeper they go into the playoffs, they have to understand the expectation level goes up. So, does experience matter? At this point, it absolutely does because you're playing now, you have the matchup that you wanted, you're playing a defending champion, and you're playing a group of guys that's already been there. As you can see last night how they celebrated each other, how they were able to do that for SGA. This is a team poised, and they're highly confident. Now, San Antonio has had a lot of success against OKC in the regular season, but now this is a movie now. This is a movie. This is going to go one game at a time, and they've been able to sit back and prepare for San Antonio and get a game plan together where they're going to take away some of these strengths and make them play to their weaknesses and still see if they can still survive OKC in that fashion.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Public reaction to Anthony Edwards' early exit from the game

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: Not feeling it. Not feeling it. What I will say, two things can be true. One, I think this is, it's kind of blown out of proportion somewhat. Obviously, we have the internet now and so people are pulling comparisons of other great players doing something similar during games. Not at the eight-minute mark though. Not at the eight-minute mark. The game was over, but my critique for Ant-Man, the game was over, and also it's eight minutes left, but they were getting handled pretty well this entire game. So it was set and done. But I think the next step for him and his maturation is understanding, wait until the end of the game and show those guys their proper respects. Also, show your proper respect to your home crowd as well for a hard-fought series in your building, a hard-fought playoff run. Give them that respect to go over and congratulate your opponent and also tell your home crowd, we also appreciate you guys. So him doing this at the eight-minute mark, that showed me that he was going to get off the floor as soon as possible as he could. So, from an optic standpoint, I didn't love it, but I also think it was blown a little out of proportion.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: I didn't like that it was on his home court either. If it was on the road, it would have almost made more sense that like, all right, I'm just going to say bye now and I'm out of here. But like, you never want to show your home crowd and your fan base that you're basically giving up, you're throwing in the towel. Although the game was over. If Cade Cunningham did this last night, it would be weird. It would be weird, but at the end of the day, the game was over and he probably doesn't want to sit there and watch them celebrate and get off the court. I just think optics-wise, business-wise, you're just one of the guys, Ant. Be there, watch the guys that didn't play a lot of opportunity, a lot of minutes early on the season, throughout this season. Watch them compete the last eight minutes of the game and finish as a unit and don't go do things as an individual. I think that's the only issue with it, but honestly, I didn't think twice about it.

quotes.speaker: Michelle Beadle
quotes.summary_phrase: Nike's Wembanyama ad trolling Anthony Edwards

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: By the way, I love a good sneaker war. I love a good social media campaign, and I love what Nike did. They took Anthony Edwards, believe this, and threw it on top of an alien logo for Wemby. How good it, by the way, and it was quick.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: Unreal. They just did something with Jalen Brunson after about the process with Joel Embiid. I love, I love a good petty. Come on. You're my biggest endorsement. I'm rocking your stuff on the biggest stage. Rep me. I love this.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: To be fair, Ant-Man started it. So, that's fair. It's all open. He started it with the commercial with the silhouettes or the block, the cartoon version of certain guys being depicted. So, it's all fun.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Naz Reid's comments on Timberwolves needing to be less moody

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: His answer's kind of weird, Lou, be less moody and more selfless. Some very interesting answer because it's weird. It's really like, we're good personnel-wise, we just have to change our personalities. What does that mean?

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: I don't know what's going on behind the scenes. Obviously, Naz Reid can speak to the moodiness and the selflessness behind the scenes. I don't know what's happening. I think they've done a great job of keeping it under wraps. Whatever's bubbling under the surface that he's speaking to, they did a great job of keeping it to themselves. But, you know,

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: Y'all do be moody though, boys.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: Oh, yeah, yeah. That's a fact. That's a fact. So I don't know what's going on there, but, from my vantage point, it looks like a team that's connected. If there's something else going on, Naz Reid is all fair for him to say and point out how he feels.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: I think I'm just more surprised at this because when I watch them play, I hear them talk with Jaden and Ant. I don't get this vibe. Not at all. So this is a little bit confusing, but also to say this again, I think emotions clearly are running high. You just got eliminated. Your season was just ended. But I don't get this vibe at all from this team, this unit. And Chris Finch, I know, is a great coach and he doesn't allow any of that outside noise or any of that pettiness linger. So I would think if this was something that was an issue, it would have been addressed way before losing Game 6 in a series. Just definitely interesting.

quotes.summary_phrase: Michelle Beadle's personal feelings and expectations for Spurs-Thunder series

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: I will tell you how I personally feel today. I feel very calm. I wouldn't even say I'm, I was nervous in the last series because I think they should have won that series. So that felt more like things were

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: You're not nervous this one?

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: I'm not nervous because, and this is, by the way, this is going to sound very anti-competitive and it feels weird for me to say out loud, but you're right. I kind of feel like I don't think they're supposed to win the series, so whatever happens is good experience. But that being said, I can't stand OKC, and I 100% hope that the San Antonio Spurs

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: If they lost to Minnesota, it would be devastating. They're a better team.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: I was legit nervous for those games.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: You lose OKC, it's like, all right, we can get them next.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: I can get over that because it's just another step in the quote-unquote experience ladder that everyone's so obsessed with. So, yeah, I'm just, but I'll say this, I'm damn excited. I am super excited. Okay, let's do it. Let's do the series predictions, Lewis. What do you got?

quotes.speaker: Michelle Beadle
quotes.summary_phrase: Michelle Beadle's rationale for Spurs winning Game 1 due to MVP presentation

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: You know what? I have Spurs winning the first game.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: Shocking.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: And here's why. Here's why. Because as we all know, SGA was presented with the MVP award yesterday, but he's going to be literally the trophy will be given to him before the game tonight.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: That's going to make him play bad.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: It's going to make Wemby play better. That's where I'm going with. It's a mental game.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: A poster of the guy that actually has the trophy that wants, now he's a back-to-back MVP and had an opportunity to start this, to continue this journey to get his second ring. He can be as petty as he want to be.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: But it's Wemby's first time being on the floor while the trophy's hanging there that he thinks he should have.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: With all due respect, this ain't about winning.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: And you don't think they hear the chatter too that this team, you don't think they've heard the chatter all year long that this team has your number? This is the only team that can beat you.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: The Thunder know that damn well.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: Why are you guys both being jerks about this?

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: I was just being realistic. We'd be saying the same thing if they were playing anybody.

text_blocks.speaker: Michelle Beadle
text_blocks.text: You also both had the Hawks winning, so I don't even take you seriously at this point. We're going to, are we taking a break? I hate them. We'll be right back. Why are you even, what's, oh my God.
